headline: Oil Whipsaws as Voters Head to the Polls
tileReason: The daily 30-year average held at 7.27% Monday as oil plunged on Iran diplomacy hopes, but a reported U.S. strike on Iran nudged Treasury yields back up on Election Day.
takeaway:
Mortgage rates are steady near six-week lows. The daily 30-year average held at 7.27% on Monday, unchanged from Friday, and Freddie Mac's weekly survey (next update Thursday) sits at 7.24%.

Monday's big story was oil. Crude fell more than 7% in a single day, with Brent settling near $104.77 a barrel and U.S. crude near $96.46, after signs that the U.S. and Iran may be moving toward talks, including an Iranian offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz under conditions. Cheaper oil eases inflation worries, and the 10-year Treasury yield, which mortgage rates tend to follow, closed near 4.89%, its lowest since mid-September.

Lenders didn't pass much of that along, though. Big tech stocks slid again on worries about heavy AI spending, which made markets choppy, and mortgage pricing barely moved.

Overnight, oil bounced back for a while. Reports that the U.S. struck Iran's Qeshm Island, near the Strait of Hormuz, pushed oil back up (Brent briefly near $106), and the 10-year yield is about 4.91% to 4.94% this morning. Oil later eased again on hopes that diplomacy survives.

Today is also Election Day. Control of Congress can shift expectations for government spending and borrowing, so markets may be jumpier than usual tonight and tomorrow. Futures markets, where traders bet on upcoming Fed decisions, still put the odds of a December Fed hike at roughly 75% to 77%.

One cushion for borrowers: mortgage rates remain unusually far above Treasuries. The Optimal Blue conforming index, which tracks rates on loans borrowers actually locked, sat 2.21% above the 10-year on Oct 30, versus a long-run average of about 1.76%, so there is room for lenders to improve pricing if markets calm down.

Next big tests: Friday's October jobs report and the Nov 10 inflation report.

fedOdds.title: Odds of a Fed hike on Dec 9
fedOdds.afterLabel: Nov 3, after Fed officials Logan and Musalem called for more hikes
fedOdds.source: CME FedWatch via Charles Schwab (Nov 3) and Trading Economics (Nov 3)
fedOdds.note: Odds of a quarter-point hike at the Dec 9 meeting were about 85% right after the Oct 28 hold, dipped to about 68% at Friday's settle by one count, and are now about 75% (Trading Economics) to 77% (CME FedWatch via Schwab). A hike is still seen as the most likely outcome.

drivers.title: Oil plunges on signs of U.S.-Iran talks
drivers.text: Crude fell more than 7% Monday, its biggest one-day drop since late July, with Brent settling near $104.77 and U.S. crude near $96.46. Iran signaled it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz under conditions, and both sides talked up the chance of a deal. Cheaper oil lowers fuel and shipping costs, which eases inflation worries, so investors bought bonds and the 10-year yield closed near 4.89%, its lowest since mid-September. Lower Treasury yields give lenders room to lower mortgage rates.

drivers.title: Reported U.S. strike on Iran's Qeshm Island
drivers.text: Overnight reports that the U.S. struck Iran's Qeshm Island, in the Strait of Hormuz, put some risk back into oil: Brent bounced to about $105–$106 before easing again on hopes that talks continue. Any sign the conflict is flaring back up raises the risk of higher energy prices and inflation, which pushes yields up. The 10-year is about 4.91%–4.94% this morning, a few hundredths above Monday's close.

drivers.title: December Fed hike still seen as likely
drivers.text: Futures put the odds of a quarter-point Fed hike on Dec 9 at roughly 75% to 77%, after two Fed officials said last week that more hikes are needed. When investors expect higher short-term rates, longer-term rates, including mortgages, have a harder time falling. Friday's jobs report and the Nov 10 inflation report will shape those odds.

drivers.title: Election Day uncertainty
drivers.text: Voters decide control of Congress today. Analysts expect Democrats to take the House and see the Senate as close. Results can shift expectations for government spending and borrowing; more borrowing means more Treasury bonds to sell, which can lift yields. Most analysts expect short-lived swings rather than a lasting move, but overnight volatility is possible.

drivers.title: Mortgage rates still far above Treasuries
drivers.text: The Optimal Blue conforming index sat 2.21% above the 10-year Treasury yield on Oct 30, compared with a long-run average of about 1.76%. Lenders did not follow Monday's drop in Treasury yields, so that gap is a cushion: if markets calm down, there is room for mortgage rates to improve even if Treasury yields stay put.

outlook.basis: Still close to a coin flip, with a slight lean toward rates staying about where they are and a very slight tilt lower. In borrowers' favor: oil fell sharply Monday on diplomacy hopes, the 10-year yield is at its lowest since mid-September, tech stocks are shaky, and mortgage rates are unusually far above the 10-year Treasury (about 2.21% vs. a long-run average near 1.76%). Working against them: a December Fed hike is still seen as likely (about 75% to 77%), inflation is well above target, and the reported strike on Iran shows how quickly oil can rebound. Big swing events: tonight's election results, the Nov 6 jobs report, the Nov 10 CPI report, and any news from Iran.
outlook.caveat: This is professional judgment from 30+ years watching these markets, not a guarantee. One oil headline or data surprise can move rates a quarter point in a day.

talkingPoints.buyers: The daily 30-year average is about 7.27%, near its lowest in six weeks and down from roughly 7.5% in early October. Oil swings tied to Iran, tonight's election results and Friday's jobs report could all move rates this week, so it's worth talking with Stuart about how locking, a float-down option (which lets you take a lower rate if rates drop after you lock), or waiting would each fit your closing date.
talkingPoints.sellers: Rates have eased a bit, which helps affordability at the margin, but buyers are still stretched above 7%. Realistic pricing, or a seller credit buyers can use to lower their rate, can help a home stand out.
talkingPoints.oneLiner: Mortgage rates are holding near six-week lows around 7.27% as oil prices swing on Iran headlines; the election and Friday's jobs report are the next big tests.
